business.name: Fictional Field Notes Studio
business.description: A test-only fictional studio that turns verified operations evidence into practical field notes for regional manufacturers.

products_services.name: Operations Field Notes
products_services.description: A fictional subscription to evidence-led operational briefs.

audiences.name: Regional manufacturing operations leaders
problems: Improvement decisions stall because local evidence is scattered across shifts.
audiences.default_problem: Improvement decisions stall because local evidence is scattered across shifts.
decision_factors: Recommendations must distinguish observed process evidence from interpretation.
objections: Generic management content does not reflect plant constraints.

positioning.statement: Fictional Field Notes Studio makes verified plant-floor learning usable without pretending one facility proves a universal rule.
expertise: Translating bounded operations evidence into decision-ready field notes.
value_propositions: Give operations leaders a concise evidence trail before recommending a process change.
proof_points: Every fictional brief carries an observation ledger and an explicit uncertainty section.

priorities: Invite qualified operations teams to compare one documented workflow.

objectives: Let the reader distinguish a local observation from a transferable mechanism.
territories: Shift handoffs, evidence quality, and bounded process improvement.

voice: Methodical and concrete: prefer an observation ledger to a dramatic claim.
editorial_principles: State the operating constraint before proposing a response.
preferred_claims: A documented local mechanism can support a bounded operational experiment.
legal_factual_reputational_restrictions: Do not identify a facility, worker, supplier, or safety incident.

calls_to_action.intent: End with the bounded operational implication.
rules: Produce no invitation or subscription language.

calls_to_action.intent: Invite the reader to compare the documented mechanism with one workflow.
rules: Ask for one workflow comparison, not a sales call.
Do not imply that the fictional evidence predicts the reader's outcome.

article_rules: Present observation, uncertainty, mechanism, and bounded experiment as separate sections.
metadata_rules: Use the operational mechanism, not a promised result, in the title.
link_rules: Link only to public technical or regulatory evidence used in the brief.
cta_rules: Place the workflow-comparison invitation before the uncertainty close.
visual_rules: Use an abstract process diagram; never show an identifiable facility.

opening_rules: Open with one observed handoff constraint, not a productivity slogan.
length_rules: Use one mechanism and one bounded implication only.
formatting_rules: Use short labeled paragraphs for observation, mechanism, and uncertainty.
link_rules: Use the verified field-note URL only when it adds the evidence trail.
cta_rules: Invite one workflow comparison without requesting a meeting.
visual_rules: Use a non-identifying process sketch sized for the LinkedIn feed.
